Title: Segment Sewing
Content: List of Contents Segment Sewing Establish Sewing Lines Directional Notches Divide Sewing Lines Based on Notches Segment Sewing - Establish Sewing Lines on segments, split by points, to connect Patterns. - Select the Segment Sewing tool from the 2D toolbar. - Or, navigate to and select Main Menu Sewing Segment Sewing. Establish Sewing Lines - Select the Segment Sewing tool from the 2D toolbar. - Navigate to the 2D window. - Click on a segment on a Pattern to establish the first half of the Sewing Line. - Then, hover the mouse over the segment where the second half of the Sewing Line will be placed to. - Drag the mouse to alter the direction of the Directional Notch as desired. - Click on the segment to establish the second half of the Sewing Line. - A pair of Sewing Lines is completed. - The Sewing Line difference will hover over the mouse cursor. - When the Sewing Line difference is larger than 1mm, the value will appear in red to alert users. Directional Notches - The direction of the Directional Notches can be changed by moving the mouse on the Sewing Lines. - To reset the Directional Notches on a pair of Sewing Lines, hit the ESC key or the Ctrl+Z keys on the keyboard. Divide Sewing Lines Based On Nothches(ver4.1.0) - Now sewing lines can be created snapping on notches, without adding segment points. - Select the Segment Sewing tool from the 2D toolbar. - Establish sewing lines based on notches.

Title: [3D Tool] Segment Sewing
Content: Objective In the 3D window, easily establish Sewing Lines on segments of Patterns or Internal Shapes/Lines. Location Main Menu Sewing Segment Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar Segment Sewing Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Segment Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar Segment Sewing All sew-able segments are bolded. All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. Navigate to the 3D window. Click once on the Pattern Outline to establish the first half of the seam. With the mouse cursor, hover over the segment to be sewn to the first half of the seam. When moving the mouse cursor, a blue point appears indicating the length of the first half of the seam. When the mouse cursor is moved close to the blue point, the Sewing Line snaps to the point (ver5.1.0). Drag the mouse to make the the Directional Notches parallel to each other. Then, click to establish the second half of the seam. Note When Directional Notches are crossed, the Sewing Lines in the 3D window are crossed as well. When Patterns are simulated at this state, either one of the Patterns is reversed and then sewn to the other Pattern. Use the shortcut to establish M:N Sewing Lines. For more detail, please reference M:N Segment Sewing.

Title: Divide Sewing Lines Based on Notches
Content: Divide Sewing Lines Based On Nothches_ver.4.1.0 - Now sewing lines can be created snapping on notches, without adding segment points. - Select the Segment Sewing tool from the 2D toolbar. - Establish sewing lines based on notches.

Title: Edit Notch Properties
Content: List of Contents Notch Properties Edit Notch Properties Notch Length Notch Properties - Edit properties of a Notch as needed. - Select the Notch tool from the 2D toolbar. - Navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern Create Notch Edit Notch Properties - Select the Notch to be modified. - The properties of the selected Notch appear in the Property Editor. Name - Rename the Notch. Type - Choose the type of the Notch. Angle - Set the degree of angle for the Notch. Perpendicular - The Notch is placed perpendicular to its segment. Custom - Decide the angle of the Notch based on its segment. Direction - This option only appears when a Notch is created in a corner. - Decided the direction of the Notch. Point (Center) - The Notch is created at the center of the corner. Segment 1 - The Notch is created towards a segment. Segment 2 - The Notch is created towards the other segment. Flip - The Notch is created on the other side of the segment. Notch Length_ver.5.0.0 and Above - Edit Notch length as desired.

Title: Delete Notch
Content: Objective Select and delete unnecessary notches. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Notch 2D Toolbar Notch Operation Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Notch 2D Toolbar Notch Select a notch to be deleted. Hit the Delete key on the keyboard. The selected notch is deleted. Or, right click on the notch and select Delete option from the right-click pop-up menu. The selected notch is deleted.

Title: Select/Move Notch
Content: List of Contents Select Move Objective Select or move notches. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Notch 2D Toolbar Notch Operation Select Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Notch 2D Toolbar Notch Click the notch created on Pattern outline or Internal Line. The notch is selected and highlighted in yellow. Move Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Notch 2D Toolbar Notch Click and drag the notch on Pattern outline or Internal Line. Release the mouse at the desired location. The selected notch is now moved. Note: To move the notch precisely with entered values, right click once while click and dragging the notch. When the Moving Distance window appears, enter the desired value to Distance Moved and select OK. The notch is moved according to the entered value. To select all notches, click Ctrl+A keys on the keyboard at the same time.

Title: Notch
Content: List of Contents Notch Create Notch Select Notch Move Notch Delete Notch Notch on Seam Allowance Notch Display Type Notch - Create, select, move, and delete Notches on Pattern outlines. - Select the Notch tool from the 2D toolbar. - Navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern Create Notch Create Notch Create Manually - Hover the mouse over the Pattern outline or Internal Line where a notch should be added. - A red point appears on the segment where the mouse is hovering over. - Click on the segment to create a Notch and it is automatically selected and highlighted in yellow. Create with Specific Numbers - To create a Notch on a specific position, right click on a segment where a notch is desired to be added. - The Notch window appears allowing you to specify location. Split into Two Lines - The line will be divided into two lines based on the reference point which was created when you hover the mouse over and right click the segment. The shorter side is indicated as Line 1, and the longer side is indicated as Line 2. - The ratio of the line to be split is 100%. The line can be divided into two lines based on the ratio. Enter the desired ratio in either Line 1 or Line 2 to split the segment into two lines. Split by Length - Divide the selected line into multiple segments according to the desired length of each segment. - Segment Length: Enter the segment length, which the whole line should be divided according to the interval. To reverse the direction that points are added, select Reverse Direction. - Number of Segments: Enter the number of segments the selected line should be divided into. - Direction: Reverse the direction that points are added. Uniform Split - Enter the number of segments the line should be divided into next to the Number of Segments option. The line is equally divided accordingly. Select Notch - Click the Notch created on a segment. - The Notch is selected and highlighted in yellow. Move Notch Move Manually - Click and drag the Notch created on a Pattern outline or an Internal Line. - Release the mouse when the Notch is moved to the desired place. - The Notch is successfully moved. Move with Specific Numbers - To move the Notch with specific numbers, right click while click-and-dragging the Notch. - Enter the desired value when the Moving Distance window appears. - The Notch is moved accordingly. Delete Notch - Select the Notch to be deleted. - Hit the Delete key on the keyboard. - Or, right click on the Notch to be deleted and select Delete option from the pop-up menu. Notch on Seam Allowance_ver5.0.0 and Above - When a notch is added, it appears on both its Pattern Outline and the seam allowance. - When a seam allowance is added to a Pattern Outline with a notch, the notch appears on the seam allowance as well. - When a notch is added to a corner with seam allowance, the notch randomly appears on either side of the seam allowance at the corner. Notch Display Type_ver5.0.0 and Above - Configure notches' 2D display options. - Navigate to the path: Main Menu Setting User Setting 2Dㅁ Notch Length Fixed to Screen : Notches are displayed in a fixed length regardless of the screen size (zoom in or out.) Note: When this option is selected, the Notch Length option disappears from the Property Editor. Actual Length : Notches's size adapts to the screen size (zoom in or out.) Note : When this option is selected, the Notch Length option appears in the Property Editor.

Title: Create Notch
Content: List of Contents Create Manually Create with Specific Values Add Point to Notch Objective Create notch on Pattern outlines as desired to improve sewing accuracy. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Notch 2D Toolbar Notch Operation Create Manually Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Hover the mouse over the Pattern outline where the notch is to be added. A notch is created and the notch properties appear in the Property Editor. Note: Right-click on a point with Edit Pattern or Edit Curve Point tool (ver 6.1) and click Add Notch, a notch is created at the point Create with Specific Values Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Right-click on the Pattern outline where notches should be added to access the pop-up window. Then, type in the desired values referring to the table below. Split Into Two Lines Line 1 / Line 2 The line will be divided into two lines based on the reference point which was created when you hover the mouse over and right click the segment. The shorter side is indicated as Line 1, and the longer side is indicated as Line 2. Enter the desired value in either Line 1 or Line 2 to split the segment into two lines. Ratio The ratio of the line to be split is 100%. The line can be divided into two lines based on the ratio. Enter the desired ratio in either Line 1 or Line 2 to split the segment into two lines. This function is often used split a line into two identical segments or to add a point at its 33.3%. Split by Length Segment Length Enter the segment length which the whole line should be divided according to the interval. To reverse the direction that points are added, select Reverse Direction. Number of Segments Enter the number of segments the selected line should be divided into. It is set as 2 by default. Direction Reverse the direction that points are added. Uniform Split Enter the number of segments the line should be divided into. The line is equally divided accordingly. The notches are created based on the chosen options. Add Point to Notch Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Right-click on the notch and click Add Point to Notch. A straight point is added to the notch. Note: If there is a seam allowance in the pattern in which the notch was created, the notch also appears in the seam allowance. In addition, if a notch is created in the corner of a pattern with seam allowance, the notch appears randomly only in one seam allowance of both seams.

Title: Internal Ellipse
Content: List of Contents Internal Ellipse Create Internal Ellipse - Create ellipse or circle within a Pattern. - Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Internal Ellipse - 2D Toolbar Internal Ellipse Create Create - Click and drag within a Pattern to create an ellipse in the 2D window. - To create a circle, hold down the Shift key while click and drag. Create with Specific Values - Click within a Pattern to create an ellipse with specific values. - The Create Ellipse window appears. Size Diameter: Set width and height of an ellipse. Radius: Set width and height of the radius of an ellipse. Circumference: Set overall circumference of an ellipse. Replicate Interval : Set the distance between each replicated ellipses. Angle : Set the angle between each replicated ellipses. Number of Shapes : Set the number of ellipses to be replicated. Position Outline : Configure the ellipses location by setting the ellipse outlines offset from the Pattern outlines left, right, top, and bottom. Center : Configure the ellipses location by setting the ellipse centers offset from the Pattern outlines left, right, top, and bottom.

Title: Create Custom Texture Image
Content: List of Contents Scan Fabric Create Repeat Match DPI (Resolution) Match Color Objective Create various custom texture images and apply to fabrics to express variety of fabric in CLO. There are four steps total to create a custom texture image: Scanning Fabric, Making Repeat, Matching DPI (Resolution), and Adjusting Color. In order to make custom texture image, image editing software, such as Pixplant, Adobe Photoshop is needed. Operation Scan Fabric Scan fabrics to digitize real world fabrics. If scanner is not available, use digital camera or cellphone camera instead. Prepare the scanner, digital camera, or cellphone camera. Spread the fabric flat on an even surface and photograph it, aligning the grainline perpendicular to the scanner or the camera's corner of the screen. Send the image to the computer. Create Repeat When a fabric is observed carefully, you can find the structure which repeats like a pattern and the structure of the fabric is often indicated as a Repeat. To express a fabric's texture, create a Repeat using the scanned image. Ways to create a Repeat differs depending on the characteristics of each fabric. Please refer to the appropriate guideline as needed. When Fabric Structure is Small and Irregular Launch PixPlant. If PixPlant is not available, please use other image editing software such as Adobe Photoshop. Left click on the Add button on the right top corner and locate the scanned image to load. Left click on the Straighten Seed &gt Click to Edit button, then select a clean part of the scanned image. Click the Generate button to create a Repeat. The area inside the square box in the Texture Canvas window represents the Repeat. Repeat procedure 3 and 4 until the desired Repeat is achieved. To recreate some portion of the Repeat, drag to select the desired part within the square box in the Texture Canvas window. When the desired Repeat is achieved, click Save. When Fabric Structure is Big and Regular Launch Adobe Photoshop or other image editing software. Find the smallest repeated area on the scanned image. Select and cut the repeated area. Copy, paste and align repeated area to check if they align naturally. When the repeated area does not align properly, showing grid lines, edit the image to make it align more smoothly. When the desired image is achieved, save the image. Note: When creating Repeats for fabrics with transparency, please select and delete the Repeat image's background and save it as PNG. Match DPI (Resolution) In order to match the image ratio of the Repeat and the real world fabric, adjust DPI (Resolution). Launch Adobe Photoshop. Open previously created Repeat. Navigate and select Main Menu &gt Image &gt Image Size. When a pop-up window appears, toggle on the Resample Image option and adjust the DPI (Resoultion) value respective to the DPI (Resolution) of the original scanned image. Open the original scanned image in Adobe Photoshop to check its DPI (Resolution) value. Save the Repeat. Match Color Match the Repeat's color respective to the real world fabric. Occasionally, photographing fabric may distort the fabric's real color. In these cases, after creating a Repeat image, adjust its color, matching the color to the original fabric's color. Open the Repeat in an image editing software such as Adobe Photoshop and adjust color as needed.

Title: Set Default Files
Content: Objective Change the default settings of the software menu according to user preference in User Settings. Upon restarting, the user settings of the software becomes the default settings. Shortcut keys, menus, graphic options, view controls, default files, font settings and other miscellaneous properties can be set in User Settings. Location Main Menu Settings User Settings Default Files Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Settings User Settings Default Files Avatar &amp Garment Project (ZPRJ) Define the file path for the default file that is loaded when starting the program. Save Thumbnails in Multiviews Save thumbnails of ZPRJ &amp ZPAC files to the default 4 sides(front, right, back, left) or load a multi-view snapshot file (MVS) and save it according to the set options. (ver 6.1) Note: When the Default 4 Views option is set, the 3D view is automatically adjusted to fit the garment, not all objects. Alvanon Permission File (APF) Define Alvanon Permission File's file path. Material Physical Property (PSP) Define the file path for the default fabric physical properties file (PSP). Texture Images Open from Assign the default path to load texture images. Refresh from Custom Folder Path Define the file path to be used when refreshing textures. Simulation Property Define the file path for the default simulation property (MSTP) file. Auto Save Time Interval (min) Adjust the time interval for auto-saving. File Type Define the file type for auto-saved files. File Path Define the saving path for auto-saved files. Custom Color Palette Define the file path for the default color palette (ACO) file. Garment Information Define the file path for the default garment information file.

Title: How can I express embroidery in CLO?
Content: There are three possible ways to express embroidery in CLO differ by the purpose and the situation. With Scanned Embroidery Without Scanned Embroidery With Scanned Embroidery When there is a scanned image of embroidery, use the Graphic tools in CLO to express embroidery. However, as expressing thick embroidery and flat embroidery methods are different, please refer to the appropriate guide below. Express Embroidery with Thickness To express embroidery with thickness, please refer to below instruction. Create a rectangle Pattern in the 2D window. Apply a new fabric to the Pattern and add texture. Create Internal Lines in the shape of embroidery on the Pattern and cut. Delete unnecessary Pattern and duplicate the Pattern outline as an Internal Shape to the 3D Garment Pattern. Sew the embroidery Pattern to the 3D Garment. Click on the fabric item applied to the embroidery Pattern in the Object Browser and change its Preset as Fusible Rigid. Also, change the Particle Distance to 5. Express Flat Embroidery Use the Graphic tools to add the embroidery image to the 3D Garment in order to express embroidery with no thickness. Without Scanned Embroidery If there is no scanned image of embroidery, use the image editing tool such as Adobe Photoshop to express embroidery effects. Then, refer to guides from the With Scanned Embroidery section. You may search how to express embroidery in image editing tools online or take a look at the reference we found below! Video Link

Title: Create Custom Texture Image for Curved Pattern
Content: List of Contents Using Adobe Photoshop Using Adobe Illustrator Objective Create custom texture image for curved pattern such as neckband. Use curved texture image when expressing lace or biz trims. Operation Using Adobe Photoshop Create custom texture image for curved pattern in Adobe Photoshop. Create a Repeat of real world fabric. Open the pattern file which the custom texture image will be applied to. Right click on the curved pattern which the custom texture image will be applied to, then select Zoom to Selected on the pop-up menu. Take a screenshot of the pattern. Launch Adobe Photoshop and open both screenshot and Repeat image. Place the Repeat image on top of the pattern image. Use the Warp function to transform the Repeat image respective to the pattern. Open a new window in Adobe Photoshop. Select, copy, and paste the modified Repeat image to the newly opened window. Save the modified Repeat image as PNG and be mindful to set the canvas size bigger than the modified Repeat image for easy application and modification in CLO. Apply the modified Repeat image to the pattern and adjust as needed to place the graphic properly. Using Adobe Illustrator Create custom texture image for curved pattern in Adobe Illustrator. Create a Repeat of real world fabric. Open the pattern file which the custom texture image will be applied to. Right click on the curved pattern which the custom texture image will be applied to, then select Zoom to Selected on the pop-up menu. Take a screenshot of the pattern. Launch Adobe Illustrator and open both screenshot and Repeat image. Trace the pattern image with the pen tool. Select the Repeat image and add as a pattern brush. Select and copy the longest segment of the traced pattern and apply the pattern brush created in procedure 6. Place the traced pattern on top of the segment with pattern brush applied. Select both pattern and segment, right click and select Make Clipping Mask. The segment with pattern brush applied will be clipped based on the pattern shape. Select the clipped pattern, navigate and select Main Menu &gt File &gt Export Selection. Designate the saving path, file name and save as PNG. Apply the modified Repeat image to the pattern and adjust as needed to place the graphic properly.

Title: [Mode] Animation
Content: Objective Record garment animation. Location Main Menu Change the mode at the top-right corner ANIMATION Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Change the mode at the top-right corner ANIMATION Animation window appears. Note: 'Complete' increases number of simulation checks to process the avatar and garment more precisely. It is recommended to set the Simulation Quality to 'Complete' to stabilize the animation as motion data increases garment collision when recording it. In addition, it provides more realistic results in fabric motion.

Title: Colorway
Content: List of Contents Run Colorway Editor Colorway Add Colorway Edit Options Change Colorway Viewer Snapshot Objective A garment project file can be saved with various colorways and imported. Location Main Menu Editor COLORWAY Operation Run Colorway Editor Click the tool/menu indicated. Colorway Editor Window appears. Colorway Add Click the Add at the top-right corner in Colorway Editor. The same colorways with the selected are newly added. By default, only items of the selected colorway are displayed in the Object Browser. Clicking the (View All Colorways) button at the top left of the Object Browser displays items of all colorways. (ver 7.3) Colorway Edit Each Click on a swatch from the colorway and change the Material. The material is changed. Click an item(Fabric, Graphic, Button, etc.) in Object Browser. Not only the material of the item, but all its properties can be edited by each colorway.(ver 7.3) Click the Update button at the left-top corner in Colorway Editor. The updates are reflected on Colorway thumbnail window. All (ver 7.3) If you want to apply items with the same properties (fabric, graphics, buttons, etc.) to all colorways at once, Hold down the Shift key to multi-select swatches. Drag and drop the item to be applied from the Object Browser to the selected swatch. It is applied to selected swatches at once. Change the item properties in the Object Browser, or select the swatch to change the properties. Changed properties are applied selected swatches at once. Options After right-clicking on the colorway or swatch, click on the menu as needed. Colorway Delete Delete the colorway. Rename Change the name of the colorway. Swatch Select All with Same Color The same color within the colorway is automatically selected. Unlink All Colorways (ver 7.3) Apply the different style for each colorway. Change Colorway Viewer Click the Show Details button at the bottom-right corner. Colorway window switches to VIEWER where you can see the colorway thumbnails only. Edit colorway is not available in VIEWER mode. Size thumbnails by controlling the scroll bar at the bottom-left corner, or arrange the thumbnails in single or multiple lines by clicking the arrangement button. Colorway Layout is changed. Snapshot Click on the Save Image button at the left-top corner. Save Image window appears. Select either 3D Window (Colorway Thumbnail) or Colorway Editor, then click OK. File Explorer window appears. Save the image after choosing the file extension, the saving path and file name.

Title: Edit Sewing
Content: List of Contents Move Properties Objective Select and move Sewing Lines or set properties. Location Main Menu Sewing Edit Sewing (B) 2D Toolbar Edit Sewing (B) Operation Move Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Click the point or segment of Sewing Line Drag it. Or, right click to enter the Distance Moved while moving. Properties Click the Sewing Line and set the properties. Properties Description Sewing Line Type Custom Angle Set the Angle and Strength of Sewing Line. Fold Angle 180 represents a flat state. The internal line is folded towards the front of the pattern as the fold angle is closer to 0, and is folded into the back of the pattern as the angle is closer to 360. Fold Strength The intensity of the fold is able to be set by adjusting the value of Fold Strength. The higher the value, the closer the fold is to the set angle. When a jacket and its lining are sewn together, the sewn area inflates due to the default sewing angle and intensity values. In this case, sets the Fold Strength to 0 to flatten the sewn boundaries. Turned Sew two layers of pattern flatly. After selecting sewing lines, press the`key on the keyboard to immediately switch the Sewing Line Type. If it is set to Turned, it is not able to adjust the Fold Angle/Strength. Tension When the 3D garment is expressed as being stretched more than the actual garment, adjust the Tension of Sewing Line. Same as actual concept, Tension is applied based on the short or long side with the Ease and Stretch options. Strength Increase or decrease the strength of the sewing tension by entering the value. The result may vary depending on the Strength even with the same Ratio value. Ratio Adjust the sewing tension's ratio to express varying drape effects by different sewing methods. Set Sublayer Assign orders to the Sewing Lines on a Pattern which folds on itself such as seam allowances and pleats in order to increase simulation stability. Reverse Direction Swap the fixed Sewing Line and the moving Sewing Line. Sublayer Decide which side of the fabric is attached to the fixed Sewing Line. Topstitch/ Puckering (ver 7.3) Applying the Topstitch and Puckering to the seam lines to create a variety of seam lines. You can save a sewing line with the properties applied and easily apply it to other sewing lines. 3D Seamline Set the direction of seam allowance. Normal Map Select an image to be used as the Normal Map. Intensity/ Thickness Adjust the intensity and thickness of the Normal Map applied to the seamline.

Title: Double-Sided Surface
Content: Objective View the front and back of the 3D Garment or Avatar without setting the fabric rendering style as Thick Textured Surface. Note: This feature is only available in ver3.2.0 and below. Location Main Menu Display Materials Double-Sided Surface Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Display Materials Double-Sided Surface The both, front and back are now being expressed the same.

Title: Simulation
Content: List of Contents Simulation Activate Simulation Simulation Presets Interactive Simulation Simulation - When the Simulation is activated, gravity will be applied to the 3D Window and patterns will be draped on the Avatar. If there are sewing lines between patterns, patterns will be sewn as draped. - Select the Simulation tool from the 3D Toolbar or navigate and select Main Menu 3D Garment Simulate. Activate Simulation - Select the Simulation tool from the 3D Toolbar. - The patterns in the 3D Window will be draped on the Avatar. - While the Simulation is activated, you can freely select and move patterns as you can in real life. Simulation Presets - Hold down the Simulation tool for about two seconds to access the child menu. - Select the desired preset. Simulate (GPU) ver5.0.0 - Select Simulate (GPU) when working on a 3D Garment. - Depending on the computer specification, the Simulation speed can increase. Simulate(Normal) - Select Simulate(Normal) when working on a 3D Garment. - When the simulation preset is set to simulate(Normal), You can work on the Garment efficiently with fast simulation speed. Simulate(Complete) - Select Simulate(Normal) after finishing a 3D Garment. - When the Simulation preset is set to Simulate (Complete), Garment simulation is more defined but the simulation speed may decrease. Simulate(Complete Nonlinear) - Select Simulate(Complete Nonlinear) after finishing a 3D Garment. - When the Simulation preset is set to Simulate (Complete Nonlinear), Garment simulation is more defined and fabric stretch is expressed more realistically. Interactive Simulation - Select the Simulation tool from the 3D Toolbar. - 3D Window is updated in real time as points or segments are edited in the 2D Window.

Title: Edit Piping
Content: List of Contents Edit Piping Select Piping Edit Length Edit Piping Properties Piping Right Click Pop-Up Menu Edit Piping - Select and edit Pipings on 3D Garments. - Select the Edit Piping tool from the 3D toolbar. - Or, navigate to and select Main Menu Materials Piping Edit Piping Select Piping - With the Edit Piping tool selected, click on the Piping on the 3D Garment. - The selected Piping will be highlighted in yellow. Edit Length - With the Edit Piping tool selected, click and drag either end of the Piping towards the direction it will be abridged or extended. Edit Piping Properties - With the Edit Piping tool or the Select/Move, click the Piping on the 3D Garment and navigate the Property Editor. - The selected Pipings properties will appear. Name - View and edit the name of the selected Piping. Line Length - View the length of the selected Piping. Width - View the length of the selected Piping. Particle Distance - View and edit the Particle Distance of the selected Piping. - The Pipings Particle Distance is set as 1.5mm by default. - Narrower the Pipings width is, smaller the Particle Distance should be. Hide - Toggle on or off the Hide checkbox to hide or show the selected Piping. - The Piping will appear translucent when the Edit Piping tool is activated, but it will disappear when other 3D tools are activated. Fabric - Change the fabric material for the selected Piping. - The options appear in the list are the fabric lists in the Object Browser. Piping Right Click Pop-Up Menu - With the Edit Piping tool or the Select/Move tool, right click on the Piping to access the right-click pop-up menu. Delete - Delete the selected Piping. - Select the Piping and hit the Delete key on the keyboard. Refresh All Piping - Re-drape all Pipings on the 3D Garment. - Use this to re-simulate Pipings that distorted while simulating the 3D Garment. Deactivate - Deactivate the selected Piping. - Right-click again on the deactivated piping. The Deactivate option should have changed to the Activate option. Select Activate to activate the piping. Freeze - Freeze the piping to exclude it from the simulation. - Right-click again on the frozen piping. The Freeze option should have changed to the Unfreeze option. Select Unfreeze to unfreeze the piping. Quadrangulate - Change the Pipings mesh structure to rectangles. Triangulate - Change the Pipings mesh structure to triangles. Hide - Hide the selected Piping. - The Piping wiil appear translucent when the Edit Piping tool is activated, but it will disappear when other 3D tools are activated. - To show the hidden Piping, select the Edit Piping tool and right click on the Piping. The Hide option should have changed to the Show option. - Select the Show option to show the selected Piping. Show All Piping - Show all hidden Pipings.

Title: Garment Rendering Style
Content: List of Contents Garment Rendering Style Textured Surface Thick Textured Surface Transparent Surface Monochrome Surface Mesh Random Colored Surface Garment Rendering Style - Check the tightness of 3D Garments with the color scale. - Hover over the third icon in the Vertical View Toggle Menu in the 3D window. Textured Surface - Only the front side of the 3D Garment will appear in its original color and the back side will appear darker to indicate the sides of the fabric. - The Garment thickness will not be expressed. Thick Textured Surface - Both front and back sides of the 3D Garment will appear in their original color and the Garment thickness will be expressed. Transparent Surface - The 3D Garment will turn translucent. Monochrome Surface - The 3D Garment will appear in black and white. - The Garment thickness will not be expressed. Mesh - The 3D Garment will appear in the mesh structure. Random Color Surface_ver5.0.0 and Above - Select the Random Color Surface icon to distinguish Patterns as they are assigned to random colors.

Title: Texture Editor
Content: List of Contents Run Texture Editor Image Layer Canvas Settings Image Properties Preview Settings Apply Texture Save Texture Image Objective Express complex graphics by overlaying multiple images. When images repeat, create seamless graphics by editing their outlines while referring to the preview. Watch Tutorial Video l Texture Editor Location Object Browser Material tabs Property Editor Open Texture Editor Operation Run Texture Editor Apply texture to the Fabric. Select the tool/menu indicated. The Texture Editor runs. The Canvas is automatically adjusted to the applied texture size. Image Layer Set the image layer in the list of layers at the bottom left of the Texture Editor. Menu Description Add Click the Add button to add the image as a new layer. Select and Import desired artboards and layers from AI/PDF files. (ver 7.1) Copy Select the added layer and click the Copy button to copy it. Lock Click the Lock button to lock the layer so that it is not edited. Layer Order Click and drag the layer to change the order. Show Click the Show(eye) icon to view or hide the layer on the window. Delete Click the Delete button to delete the layer. Rename Double-click the name of the layer to edit it and press enter to apply it. Canvas Setting At the top of the texture editor, set up the canvas as needed. Menu Description Size Set the width and height of the canvas. Adjust the canvas size to the size of a specific image by right-clicking of the layer. (ver 7.1) Unit Set the units of the canvas and image. PPI (Pixels) Set the resolution of the canvas. Transparent Background Set the image to a Transparent Background. Image properties Set the Image properties of the selected layer in the Properties list at the bottom right of the Texture Editor. Properties Description Paint Blend Mix the selected layer with the bottom layer. Color Set the color of the image. Color Switch Number Set the number of colors to extract from the image. Sub Color Click the extracted color chip to change it to the different color. Opacity Adjust the Opacity of the image. Desaturate Remove the color while maintaining the pattern or texture of the texture image and change it to another color. Repeat Repeat Repeat the image. Space / Shift Adjust the space and shift value between repeated textures. Extend to Other Side If the image intersects with the grid, extend it to the other side. Transformation Pivot Set the Pivot position of the image. Position Move the image based on the Position of the Pivot. Size/Angle Set the size and angle of the image. Reset Click the Reset button for the Position, Size and Angle properties to revert back to the original image. Preview Settings Click the Preview Settings in the upper right corner of the Texture Editor. The Preview Settings window appears. Set the options below. Menu Description Show Grid View or hide the grid. Occlude Opacity Set the Opacity of repeated images in the Preview window. Apply Texture When the texture editing is complete, click the Apply &amp Close button at the bottom right of the Texture Editor. The edited texture is applied. Save Texture Image Click Save Image at the bottom left of the Texture Editor window. Save Images window appears. Select the image to save and click OK. The file explorer window appears. Select the folder to save the image. The image is saved as modified in the Texture Editor.

Title: Edit Fabric (Print Layout Mode)
Content: List of Contents Roll Width Description Texture Objective Edit Fabric directly in Print Layout Mode. Location Main Menu Materials Edit Texture 3D Toolbar Edit Texture Operation Roll Width Navigate to Print Layout mode. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Edit Texture 3D Toolbar Edit Texture Select the Fabric with the print/texture to be edited. The selected Fabric print/texture properties appear in the Property Editor. Adjust roll Width and Position (ver5.0.0.) under the Roll option. Select a preset number from a drop-down menu next to the Width option. Or, use the in and mm options to insert desired value. Use the Position option to adjust the Fabric's placement (ver5.0.0.) The Roll Width is changed according to the selected or entered value. Description Navigate to Print Layout mode. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Edit Texture 3D Toolbar Edit Texture Select the Fabric with the print/texture to be edited. The selected Fabric print/texture properties appear in the Property Editor. Enter the information for the Fabric file in Description. Texture Navigate to Print Layout mode. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Edit Texture 3D Toolbar Edit Texture Select the patterns to be edited in the 3D window. The texture Gizmo and grainline appear as in Simulation mode. Edit texture as needed. Also adjust Texture, Color, and Specular Color, as needed. Note: Pattern placement is maintained even after texture modification or replacement (ver4.0.0).

Title: Bond
Content: Objective Add bonding effect on desired parts of a Pattern or all Patterns (ver2.3.0). Location Property Editor (Internal Shapes/Pattern Only) Bond/Skive Bond Operation Select a pattern or an internal shape to express bonding with Edit Pattern or Transform Pattern tools. Its properties appear in the Property Editor. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor (Internal Shapes/Pattern Only) Bond/Skive Bond The select Pattern/Internal Shape is now being displayed in a semi-transparent orange color. By default, the same physical property as the selected Pattern/Internal Shape is now being added to the selected Pattern/Internal Shape. Activate the Simulate. The bonded area is now being displayed stiffer as if an interlining has been fused. Repeat the first step again. In the Property Editor, select a desired preset to change its physical property. For more detailed adjustments, click on Detail. The lists on the drop-down menu are the same as Fabric's.

Title: Fabric_Color
Content: List of Contents Color Change color Change color with Eyedropper Color - Change the color of the fabric. Change Color - When changing the Color, select the desired item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches. The selected items properties will appear in the Property Editor. - Navigate to the Property Editor and locate the Color chip next to the Color option, under the Material section. - Click on the Color chip to open the Color window to assign the desired Color to the selected item. - Click the desired Color. The selected Color will be applied to the item. - Click OK to complete. Change Color with Eyedropper - When changing the Color, select the desired item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches. The selected items properties will appear in the Property Editor. - Navigate to the Property Editor and locate the Color chip next to the Color option, under the Material section. - Click on the Color chip to open the Color window. - Select the Eyedropper tool. - Drag the mouse cursor outside the Color window. When the cursor changes to an Eyedropper, click on the spot anywhere in the window to extract the desired color. - The color of the selected spot will appear in the Color window. - Select OK to complete. - The chosen Color will be assigned to the selected item.

Title: Garment Information
Content: List of Contents Garment Information Enter Default Garment Information Add Category Reorder Category Delete Category Save Garment Information Garment Information - Easily record and check necessary information for a 3D Garment. - Main Menu File Information Garment. Enter Default Garment Information - Information fields such as Style No, Name, Description, Fabric, Colorway and Size appear in the Garment Information window by default. - Type in appropriate information for each category. - Toggle on the Display When Garment File Loads option to load the Garment Information every the file opens. - To save the information, click OK. Add Category - Click the Edit button on the right top corner to add more categories. - When it shifts to the edit mode, click the Add button on the right top corner. - When the new category is added, select the desired category type with the drop-down menu. - Click the Exit button to finish editing. Reorder Category - Click the Edit button on the right top corner to reorder categories. - When it shifts to the edit mode, click and drag the category to the desired placement. - The selected category is moved to where the mouse is released. - Click the Exit button to finish editing. Delete Category - Click the Edit button on the right top corner to delete categories. When it shifts to the edit mode, click the Delete button next to the category to be removed. - Click the Exit button to finish editing. Save Garment Information - Click the Edit button on the right top corner to delete categories. - Use the Save button on the right top corner to save category list, order, and contents. - Saved information can be loaded by using the Open button as well.

Title: Edit Binding Properties
Content: List of Contents Binding Properties Edit Binding Properties Binding Properties - Adjust properties for Binidngs. - Select the Select Binding tool from the 3D toolbar. Note: Binding can also be selected with the Select/Move tool from the 3D toolbar. Edit Binding Properties - When the Binding tool is selected, the 3D garment turns translucent and segments with Binding appear in grey. - Select the Binding to be edited. - Selected Bindings properties appear in the Property Editor. Name Rename Bindings name. Line Length Check Bindings length. However, it cannot be changed from the Property Editor. Type Under Express Inside Bindings. Over Bindings are placed over the Patterns. Dimension Width Adjust selected Bindings width (1~50mm). Particle Distance Edit selected Bindings Particle Distance (1~20mm). Fabric Assign Fabric to the Binding. Fabric styles in the Fabric Object Browser appear in a list. Topstitch Add Topstitch to the Binding. Only Topstitches in the Topstitch Object Browser appears for the options. Sewing Line Type Edit Bindings Sewing Line Type.

Title: Desaturation
Content: Desaturation - Remove the color of the fabric, but maintain its Pattern and texture to apply a different color to the fabric. - Select the desired fabric item from the Object Browser to remove its color. - Navigate to the Property Editor and expand the Material Texture to see its child menus. - Toggle on the Desaturation. - The fabrics color will be removed but its Pattern and texture will be remained. - Adjust the Shadow Intensity and Shadow Brightness to edit the textures shadow.

Title: Adjust Stretch-Weft/Warp, Shear
Content: Objective Use the Weft, Warp and Shear intensities to show the resistance against the horizontal, vertical and diagonal elasticity according to the 2D window. Increasing the Shear intensity to the same ratio as the Weft and Warp intensities, is going to express materials that creases easily such as cotton and denim. On the other hand, decreasing the intensity value is going to express more elastic materials such as silk and jersey. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Physical Property Detail Stretch-Weft/Warp, Shear

Title: Edit Binding Properties
Content: List of Contents Binding Properties Edit Binding Properties Binding Properties - Adjust properties for Binidngs. - Select the Select Binding tool from the 3D toolbar. Note: Binding can also be selected with the Select/Move tool from the 3D toolbar. Edit Binding Properties - When the Binding tool is selected, the 3D garment turns translucent and segments with Binding appear in grey. - Select the Binding to be edited. - Selected Bindings properties appear in the Property Editor. Name : Rename Bindings name. Type: Place the Binding below or above the Pattern. Line Length: Check Bindings length. However, it cannot be changed from the Property Editor. Width (mm): Adjust selected Bindings width (1~30mm). Length (%): Adjust selected Binding's length with percentage (50~200%) (ver5.0.0.) Length (in): Adjust selected Binding's length with a specific value. When adjusting the Binding with a specific value, the unit follows the program's default unit (ver5.0.0.) Particle Distance (mm): Edit selected Bindings Particle Distance (1~20mm). Add'l Thickness - Collision (mm): Adjust the Add'l Thickness - Collision value of each Binding (ver5.0.0.) Fabric: Assign Fabric to the Binding. Fabric styles in the Fabric Object Browser appear in a list. Topstitch: Apply Topstitch on top of the Binding. All Topstitch styles added in the Object Browser appear as options (ver4.2.0.) Sewing Line Type: Edit Bindings Sewing Line Type.

Title: Adjust Friction Coefficient
Content: Objective Use this function to adjust the friction of Garments. The Friction Coefficient affects the friction between a Garment and another Garment. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Physical Property Detail Friction
